description: Law-vector families this repository emits (Phase 564). SELF-ENUMERATED, as apply/ and refusals/ are, and distinct from the shared corpus's laws/manifest.json, which indexes these files beside another producer's and carries no adoption. `adoption` is per host and is DATA: a host whose entry reads `proposed` reports the family BY NAME rather than skipping it, and flips its own entry in the change-set that lands its leg. This manifest is authoritative for the vector counts.

families.description: The (input, expected) pairs Fuaran.Core.Conformance.capabilityLaws draws from `seed` over `iterations` iterations, computed by calling the pinned kit. A host reproduces the sample with its own ConfRng: per iteration draw intBelow(50) = lo, intBelow(50) = span (hi = lo + span + 1), intBelow(1000) = the captured value, and build one capability per iteration over a single required value hole at address `h0` named `x` in IntRange(lo, hi) with effect readsHost and the determinism set of the (i mod 7)th non-empty subset of {clock, random, network} in mask order (mask 1..7, bit 0 clock, bit 1 random, bit 2 network; the label names the members in that order joined by `+`). `capability` and `declaration` members carry a canonical capability declaration as a JSON STRING — decode it with the host's capability codec. Each argument is `{"name", "value"}`, keyed by the qualified name of the hole it binds (Phase 712, DECISIONS.md D281), never by the hole's address: the vectors bind `x`, and the address `h0` binds nothing. `validateArgs` vectors expect accept, or reject with a named error class and the `name` of the offending argument; each bound of the range is pinned at it and one past it (`accept` at lo, `at-upper-bound` at hi, `past-lower-bound` at lo - 1, `out-of-space` at hi + 1: the range is inclusive at both ends). `invocationKey` vectors expect the effect-identity key a non-deterministic invocation is journalled under, its determinism tag, and the value the replay must return byte-identically. `declarationRoundTrip` expects decode-then-encode to return the input bytes. `registryEnumerate` expects id-sorted enumeration regardless of insertion order (the declarations are given in insertion order). Since Phase 642 every capability declares its `result`: IntRange(0, 999) on an even iteration and `{"$type":"nothing"}` on an odd one. `declarationRefused` vectors expect the declaration reader to reject with a decode `code` and the `path` to the fault: a declaration without `result` is MissingField at [result], and one whose result space is empty is OutOfRange at [result]. `pipelineTypeCheck` vectors register the capability alone and type-check the given one-node pipeline: accept, or reject `pipelineOutputContradicts` naming the node and the capability when the node's declared output does not admit the capability's result (or the capability answers nothing).

The exact decimal (D72): authored inputs over every behaviour a host mirrors, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit. No seed: nothing is drawn. Every vector expects `verdict` accept or reject; a reject names its class. `canonical` reads `text` (the grammar -?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? with ASCII digits only) and expects the canonical form: no leading zero, no trailing fraction zero, no point on a whole number, no sign on zero. `compare` expects the numeric `order` of `a` and `b` as -1, 0 or 1. `add` expects the exact canonical `sum`. `toFloat` expects the nearest double in the canonical float layout, and rejects a value past the float range rather than answering an infinity. `codecDecode` decodes a one-column decimal `document` and expects its canonical re-encoding; a decimal is a JSON string on the wire, an integer token is read exactly, and a fractional token or a whole token past 2^53 is refused. `codecEncode` builds column `c` of type decimal from `cells` ({kind, text}; a null cell has no text) and expects the guarded encode's canonical bytes, or the refusal of a cell whose text is not canonical. `aggregate` folds `fn` over the same column and expects the result cell's token (`m:` a decimal, `i:` an int, `f:` a float): Sum is exact, Min and Max return the winning cell as it stands, Mean, Median and StdDev (the population form) read each value at its nearest double, and a value past the float range is refused for them.

The schema field (Phase 427): a column's name and type, and the metadata that says what it means — an optional unit (the canonical text of a unit the unit algebra parses), a label, a description, and an extension object of string members a host preserves verbatim. Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. `fieldEncode` builds a field from its members (`name`, `type`, and whichever of `unit`, `label`, `description`, `ext` are given) and expects the schema entry's canonical bytes: the members the field states and no other, keys sorted, so an entry without metadata is `{name, type}`. `codecDecode` decodes a zero-row `document` and expects its canonical re-encoding — a parseable unit spelling is read to the unit and written back canonical, an empty `ext` is dropped, an unknown member is read past — or the refusal's class: a unit the algebra does not parse, a non-string `unit`, `label` or `description`, an `ext` that is not an object, and an `ext` member that is not a string are each `MalformedShape`. `fingerprint` reads a `schema` (an array of entries) and expects its FNV-1a fingerprint: a schema without metadata has the fingerprint it had before this phase, and metadata moves it. `delta` reads `old` and `target` schemas and expects the canonical bytes of the delta between them (`amended` present only when a member moved) and `patched`, the schema replaying that delta over `old` yields, which is `target`. `classify` reads the same pair and `dependsOn` and expects `compat`: `breaking` when a depended-on column's stated unit was replaced or withdrawn (or it was removed or narrowed), `unknown` when only a depended-on column's extension member moved, else `compatible`.

The (input, expected) pairs Fuaran.Core.Conformance.propagationEvalLaws draws from `seed` over `iterations` iterations (and dirtyPropagationLaws' fixed cyclic graph), computed by calling the pinned kit. A host reproduces the sample with its own ConfRng, one cursor across all iterations: per iteration draw intBelow(6) + 2 = n, the ids `0` .. `n-1`; for each node k ascending, intBelow(3) for each j < k ascending, k reading j where it is 0; intBelow(100) per node ascending, its base; intBelow(n), the changed node, whose base grows by 1000. Every input carries the graph as `deps` (each id to the ids it reads), so the vectors also replay without the draw. The evaluator is value(n) = base(n) + the sum of value(r) over n's declared reads r, a read that resolves to nothing counting 0. `dirtySet` expects the changed ids and every node that transitively reads one, sorted. `evaluationOrder` expects the order the reference walks — Tarjan over the ids in ascending ordinal order, each node's reads ascending, dependencies first — and the cyclic groups, each sorted; a host whose sort breaks ties differently instead holds its own order to the certificate: no id twice, order and cycles partitioning the ids, every acyclic read earlier. `evalFrom` re-evaluates `changedBase` incrementally over the prior `eval` of `base`: it expects the values, which equal a full evaluation of `changedBase`, and `recomputed`, the nodes the evaluator was invoked on, which is exactly the dirty set — or, for a changed id the graph does not hold, the evalUnknownChange refusal naming it. `undeclaredRead` makes `node` also read `read`, which it never declared: both eval and evalFrom (with `node` changed) refuse with evalUndeclaredRead naming the node and the read, whether the read names a node of the graph or an id it does not hold. Every vector's `answeredBy` is ["reference", "model:Propagation"]: the export also ran the extracted F* model (proofs/Propagation.fst) on the input and found the same answer.

The canonical-form declarations of an IDL vocabulary (Phase 539): a member's ALIASES (retired spellings a decoder accepts and normalises to the canonical name, the canonical spelling winning when both are present, otherwise the first alias in declared order), an enum case's aliases (lenient wire strings that decode to the case and re-encode as its canonical string), a member's PRESENCE condition (`whenPresent` / `whenAbsent` an Optional sibling, or `whenEquals` a sibling's scalar value, an absent OmitDefault sibling holding its default; a member whose condition fails is absent from the canonical form, so a decoder drops it UNREAD, whatever its value, ill-typed included, and it decodes as its optionality's absence), and an empty-map or JSON default literal (omitted at its default, compared by canonical bytes). `vocabulary` is the fixture's idl.json; each vector reads `document` (a node over that vocabulary) and expects `expected`, the canonical bytes the reference decodes and re-encodes it to, computed by calling the pinned kit.

The capability registry's gate, decision context and grant (Phase 638, DECISIONS.md D249), as data a port decides from (Phase 650, D255). Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. `registry` holds the three capability declarations, each a canonical declaration as a JSON string. `contexts` names the two decision contexts, opaque labels. Each argument is `{"name", "value"}`, keyed by the qualified name of the hole it binds (Phase 712, DECISIONS.md D281); each hole here is named as it is addressed. `gates` is the gate table in the order the registry runs it: a gate answers the `decision` of its rule for the (context, capability) pair, and `allow` for any pair it has no rule for. The registry's decision is the join over every gate in order (allow < needsApproval < deny, a deny keeping its message and alternatives), and the gate that made it is the FIRST gate whose decision has the greatest rank; `policy` is "" when every gate allows. `invocationIdentity` vectors expect the identity a grant is bound to: the fields id, then for each binding its hole's qualified name and its value's canonical spelling in its hole's space (an integer without sign or leading zeros, a number in its shortest round-trip form, a string as given), the bindings sorted by name (ordinal), each field written with every U+0010 and U+0001 it holds preceded by U+0010, then terminated by U+0001; no hash is taken. `grantCovers` vectors expect whether a presented grant (the `grant` member, an identity; absent when none is presented) is for exactly this invocation: it is when the two identities are equal as strings. `decideNamed` vectors expect the registry's named decision for an invocation under a context with a grant presented: `decided` with the deciding gate and the decision, where a needsApproval a covering grant lifts is `allow` and keeps the gate's name, and no grant lifts a deny; or, where no gate decided, `refused` with the refusal a dispatch gives (an unregistered id is `noSuchCapability` with the registered ids, an argument out of its space `argOutOfSpace` with its `name`). `dispatch` vectors expect `performed` when the performer ran, exactly once, or `refused` with the refusal: `policyRefused` naming the gate with its reason and alternatives for a deny, `approvalRequired` naming the gate for a needsApproval no grant lifts, `noSuchCapability` for an unregistered id whatever is presented; a refused dispatch never runs the performer. `referenceOnly` names the cases no extracted model answers, with the reason.

The document value space (Phase 644, DECISIONS.md D260), through the cases of capability-laws.json: `validateArgs`, `invocationKey`, `declarationRoundTrip` and `pipelineTypeCheck`, each read exactly as that file describes it. Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. Every vector is stated over one capability, `cap-document`: a single required hole at address `d0` named `order` in the document space of type `Order`, answering a document of type `Receipt`. `capability` and `declaration` members carry a canonical capability declaration as a JSON STRING, in which a document space is `{"$type":"document"}` with an optional `documentType`. A document argument is a member exactly when it is well-formed JSON with a canonical rendering of its own: it parses with no `null`, and holds no repeated member, no ill-formed string and no number a finite float cannot spell. The type name is carried and never read. An argument is keyed by its hole's qualified name, `order`, never by the address `d0` (Phase 712, DECISIONS.md D281). An argument that is no document is `argOutOfSpace` naming it. The two `document-key-*` vectors present ONE document in two spellings (members out of order, white space, a float with a trailing zero, a control character by its short escape) and expect one key: an argument in a document space is keyed by its cross-host canonical text (members sorted, no white space, the canonical float layout, every control character as `\u00xx`). They carry no `capturedValue`. The `document-pipeline-output-*` vectors pin the space relation: a document result is admitted by a declared output of the same type or of no type, and by no other document type, no scalar space and no tree space.

The query registry's grant (Phase 651, DECISIONS.md D261): the identity a grant for a read is bound to, and whether a presented grant covers a read. Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. `registry` holds the queries the vectors read, each a canonical declaration as a JSON string. A binding is `{name, cell}`, a cell `{kind, text}` with no text for a null (a float's text is its shortest round-trip form, a boolean's `true` or `false`). `invocationIdentity` vectors expect the identity: the fields id; then, when the declaration declares a filter, the three fields "", `w` and the canonical text of its `where` member, and when it declares an order, "", `o` and the canonical text of its `orderBy` member, filter first; then for each binding, sorted by name (ordinal), its name, its kind's tag (`i` int, `f` float, `b` bool, `s` string, `d` date, `t` timestamp, `m` decimal, `n` null) and its payload (an integer's decimal digits, a float's shortest round-trip text, `1` or `0` for a boolean, a string, date, timestamp or decimal as given, empty for a null); each field written with every U+0010 and U+0001 it holds preceded by U+0010, then terminated by U+0001; no hash is taken. A cell is identified by its kind, so an integer bound to a float parameter and the float of the same value are two reads. `grantCovers` vectors expect whether a presented grant (the `grant` member, an identity; absent when none is presented) is for exactly this read: it is when the two identities are equal as strings. A `pageToken` member names the page the read is dispatched for: it is in neither identity, so a grant for a read covers every page of it, and a page's capture key is no grant. The gate's decision and dispatch are the gate family's (capability-gate-laws.json): one function decides at both registries.

The refusals a query declaration and a read of it meet (Phase 680, DECISIONS.md D263). Authored inputs, each `expected` computed by calling the pinned kit; no seed. `registry` holds the queries the vectors read, each a canonical declaration as a JSON string, in id order. `gates` is the gate table the registry runs: a gate answers the `decision` of its rule for a query, and `allow` for a query it has no rule for. Every refusal but the reader's is pinned as its query-error document, an object under `error`, as the seam codec writes it (the document seam-refusals.json certifies a reader of); no sentence is pinned. `declarationRefused` vectors read `declaration`, a declaration's text, with the declaration reader (lenient: an unknown member is read past) and expect `accept`, or `reject` with the decode `code` and the `path` to the fault: the members are read in the order $type, id, params, resultSchema, effect, timeoutMs, pageSize, where, orderBy, source, and the admission gate last, whose refusal is OutOfRange at the gate's path; timeoutMs and pageSize are positive integers, and one that is not is OutOfRange at its member (Phase 685); the parser refuses every null and every number past the finite double range, InvalidJson at the root. `admissionFault` and `register` vectors state a declaration as DATA, because two of the gate's refusals no text can carry: `query` names a declaration of `registry`, and `id` (a string), `params` (a list of {name, type, required}), `where` (a list of {predicate, column}, with `cell` for a comparison and `text` for contains), `orderBy` (a list of {column, direction}) and `source` (Phase 688: an embedded table, `schema` a list of {name, type} and `columns` a list of {name, type, cells}, every cell present, a name free to repeat in either list, each column held as stated by its type's builder), when present, replace its own. A cell is {kind, text}, no text for a null, its text as it stands and never canonicalised (a float's is its shortest round-trip form, a non-finite float's the token in quotes, as the canonical float layout writes it). `admissionFault` vectors hold the declaration to the admission gate and expect `admitted`, or `refused` with `at`, the path to the member at fault, and `error`: a source table the column layer refuses at [source], illFormedSource with that layer's reason (a valid table in any column order is admitted); then a parameter declared twice at [params]; then each predicate in turn at [where, i] (an undeclared column, then contains off a string column, then a null literal, then a literal of another type, with no widening and a timestamp fitting a column at least as fine as its own unit, then a literal its column cannot carry, with the column layer's reason); then each order key at [orderBy, i] (an undeclared column, then a column named before). `register` vectors register the declaration into the registry and expect `registered`, or `refused` with `error`: an id the registry holds is refused before the gate. `validateParams` vectors hold `args` (a list of {name, cell}) to `query`'s parameters and expect `accept`, or `reject` with the first refusal: a name bound twice; then per argument in order an unknown name or a cell that does not widen to its parameter's type (an int fills a float or a decimal, a null fills any); then every required name left out; then every required name bound only to null. `dispatch` vectors dispatch a read through the registry, a `grant` (an identity, as query-grant-laws.json writes one) presented or not, and expect `performed` when the resolver ran, exactly once, or `refused` with `error`: an unregistered id whatever is presented, then validation, then the gate, a deny lifted by no grant and a needsApproval by a grant for exactly this read only. `referenceOnly` names the vectors no extracted model answers (a case whole, or the `vectors` it lists), with the reason; every other vector's `answeredBy` names the query model. `unreached` names each case of QueryError no vector raises, with what raises it and why.
